about: The explainer video's script, in chapters (`beats`), each with its lines. `text` is what the captions show; `say`, where given, is what the voice says instead (numbers and names written for speaking); `em` lists the phrases the frame lights in petrol as they are spoken. `lead` is the silence before a chapter's first line, `post` the pause after a line, `tail` the hold after a chapter's last line, all in seconds; `min` is a chapter's least length. narrate.py voices the lines (Kokoro, af_heart); film.js draws each chapter and times its parts by the voice's own words. The pacing follows PACING.md: one breath a sentence, one idea a line.

lines.text: stretto reads ahead of your agent.
Here's what it reads, where its lookups come from, and what it saves.
An agent works in turns.
On each turn, a model reads the whole conversation, then picks one next step.
It answers, or it calls a tool.
Each turn costs seconds and thousands of tokens. A task can take ten or twenty.
Look closely, and many turns are decided before they begin.
This customer's record lists two orders.
So the next two turns will read those two orders.
The tools made that choice. The model spends a turn typing it out.
stretto sits between the agent and its tools, as an MCP proxy.
When a result names what comes next, stretto makes those reads at once.
They ride back inside the result the agent asked for.
So the agent skips those turns. No new tools, and the same prompt.
A flow only reads. It calls no tool the server marks as a write.
A lookup the agent doesn't use is a detour. It costs tokens, and changes no state.
The lookups come from your agent's own recorded sessions.
stretto counts which reads follow each call, and where each argument came from.
The result is a flow: a small file you can read, review and diff.
In replay, ten of an agent's own sessions give most of what all of them do.
em: ten of an agent's own sessions

lines.text: The console puts your servers, sessions, flows and jobs in one place.
A session shows each call, the lookups the flow made after it, and why.
A flow shows its graph, and what would change at another threshold.
Each lookup weighs two costs: a turn saved, against a detour.
stretto makes it when the chance it's used before the next write clears the line.
Measured live on τ²-bench, that line sits at about thirty percent.
